newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Short covering post-auction helps OLOs higher.
newsitem.headline: Short covering post-auction helps OLOs higher.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds edged higher in late trade on Tuesday, aided by a strong performance in Bunds and short-covering after a non-competitive OLO auction, dealers said.
"We are just following Bunds around," said one trader. "Belgian seems to be very strong at the moment. We've seen good buying interest in the longer end."

Adding to the upbeat peformance was a relatively small non-competitive OLO bond auction. Dealers said the finance ministry trimmed the amount offered, prompting a bout of short-covering in afternoon dealings.
Some traders said the upturn in prices also reflected a strong opening to U.S. market, which was aided by a return of overseas investors.
In early trading the U.S. benchmark 6.75 percent 30-year bond opened up 13/32 to yield 6.97 percent.
But others were less convinced and expressed worry that the Federal Reserve might have fallen behind in its battle against inflation.
"I'm still a bit worried about the U.S.," said one trader. "I think the Fed is running a bit behind the curve at the moment."
Earlier, the Belgian Treasury auctioned three-month T-bills at an average yield of 3.14 percent, down from 3.29 percent last week.
At its non-competitive OLO auction, meanwhile, the Treasury sold 9.235 billion worth of securities.
